title: Where You Go
subtitle: Ruth in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin: Ruth is a short story about a famine, three funerals, a foreign widow, and a field of barley. By the last page, an empty house is full and a family line runs toward David. This book walks through its four chapters in twenty-four short poems. Each poem sits beside a picture and under a single line of Scripture.

parts.title: Empty
parts.epigraph: I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty.
parts.lightHint: Beside the stone milestone where two roads meet toward Bethlehem
parts.zh_epigraph: 我满载而归，耶和华又带我空手而归。

parts.title: Gleaning
parts.epigraph: Who has not abandoned his kindness to the living and to the dead.
parts.lightHint: Among the golden barley sheaves and the cool water jars
parts.zh_epigraph: 谁没有放弃对生者和死者的仁慈。

parts.title: The Threshing Floor
parts.epigraph: Shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?
parts.lightHint: By the winnowing floor where the mantle of refuge is spread
parts.zh_epigraph: 我岂不应为你寻求安息，使你得福吗？

parts.title: Redeemed
parts.epigraph: Blessed be Yahweh, who has not left you today without a near kinsman.
parts.lightName: Light of the House of Bread
parts.lightHint: Near the town gate elders’ bench before the Finale Plaza
parts.zh_epigraph: 耶和华是应当称颂的，他今天没有离开你，没有让你失去一个至亲。

paintings.title: house of bread
paintings.epigraph: “there was a famine in the land”
paintings.poem:
it begins with an empty field
in a town called House of Bread.

a man looks at the dust
and makes the choice
hungry men have always made:

he packs what he can carry,
takes his wife and two sons,
and walks toward the bread
he can see.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Ruth 1:1 points us to the daily loaf broken in the hand and whispers, “a man looks at the dust and makes the choice hungry men have always made: he packs what he can carry, takes his wife and two sons, and walks toward the bread he can see.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
它以一个空字段开始
在一个叫“面包之家”的小镇里。

一个人看着灰尘
并做出选择
饥饿的人们总是做出：

他打包了他能携带的东西，
带着他的妻子和两个儿子，
然后走向面包
他能看到。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界以速度和噪音来衡量生命，然而《路得记》1章1节向我们指出了每天在手中掰开的面包，并低语道：“一个人看着尘土，做出了饥饿者总是做出的选择：他收拾好他能携带的东西，带着他的妻子和两个儿子，走向他能看到的面包。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “那地发生饥荒”

paintings.title: one breath
paintings.epigraph: “the woman was bereaved of her two children and of her husband”
paintings.poem:
first her husband.
then, ten years on,
both of her sons.

the text says it in one breath,
the way grief does—
too heavy to linger on,
too heavy to put down.

she is left
with two daughters-in-law,
a word for what she is now,
and no word
for what comes next.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “she is left with two daughters-in-law, a word for what she is now, and no word for what comes next.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
首先是她的丈夫。
然后，十年过去了，
她的两个儿子。

文字一口气说完，
就像悲伤一样——
太沉重而无法停留，
太重了，放不下。

她被留下了
带着两个儿媳妇，
一句话形容她现在的样子
没有一句话
接下来会发生什么。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以一个安静的转折结束：“她只剩下两个儿媳妇，只字不提她现在的样子，不言不语未来的事。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这名妇女失去了她的两个孩子和她的丈夫”

paintings.title: news from home
paintings.epigraph: “Yahweh had visited his people in giving them bread”
paintings.poem:
news travels even to Moab:
there is bread in Bethlehem again.

no angel, no voice from heaven—
just word from a traveler,
a harvest on the other side of the hills.

sometimes this is how God visits:
through ordinary news
that it is time
to go home.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “sometimes this is how God visits: through ordinary news that it is time to go home” (Ruth 1:6) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
消息甚至传到了摩押：
伯利恒又有面包了。

没有天使，没有来自天堂的声音——
只是一位旅行者的一句话，
山的另一边正在收获。

有时上帝就是这样拜访的：
通过普通新闻
现在是时候了
回家。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时，一句话可以在封闭的房间里打开一扇窗：“有时，神临到的时候，借着平常的消息，告诉我们该回家了”（路得记1:6）如何解答你最近一直在思考的一个问题？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶和华眷顾他的子民，赐给他们面包”

paintings.title: where you go
paintings.epigraph: “where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay”
paintings.poem:
Orpah kissed her and went back.
no one blames her.
it was the sensible road.

but Ruth stayed—

your road, my road.
your roof, my roof.
your people, my people.
your God, my God.

she had nothing to gain
and everything to lose,
and she chose
an old woman's empty hands.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “where you go” (Ruth 1:14–17): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “she had nothing to gain and everything to lose, and she chose an old woman's empty hands”?
paintings.zh_poem:
奥尔帕吻了她一下就回去了。
没有人责怪她。
这是明智的道路。

但露丝留下来了——

你的路，我的路。
你的屋顶，我的屋顶。
你的人民，我的人民。
你的上帝，我的上帝。

她没有什么可得到的
以及失去的一切，
她选择了
老妇人两手空空。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“你要去哪里”之前（路得记1:14-17），请张开你的双手：当你听到“她一无所获，却又失去一切，却选择了一个老太婆的空空双手”时，你紧握的是什么东西松开了？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你去哪里，我就去哪里；你留哪里，我就留哪里”

paintings.title: call me bitter
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara”
paintings.poem:
the whole town came out:
is this Naomi?

don't call me pleasant, she said.
call me bitter.
I went out full
and came home empty.

she said it plainly, about God,
and the book keeps her words
without correcting them.

there is room in Scripture
for a woman
not ready yet
to say thank you.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Ruth 1:19–21 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “there is room in Scripture for a woman not ready yet to say thank you” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
全镇的人都出来了：
这是娜奥米吗？

别说我讨人喜欢，她说。
请叫我苦涩。
我满载而归
然后空手而归。

她坦白地说，关于上帝，
这本书保留了她的话
而不纠正它们。

圣经中有空间
对于一个女人
还没准备好
说声谢谢。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经在路得记 1 章 19-21 节中记住这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻的印象，而是为了让我们坚定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到过“圣经中有地方让一个还没有准备好说谢谢的女人”这个真理？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “别叫我内奥米。叫我玛拉”

paintings.title: barley harvest
paintings.epigraph: “They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.”
paintings.poem:
she said she came home empty.
but look who walked beside her.

and look at the fields—
the first barley bending gold
the very season they arrived.

the story doesn't argue with her grief.
it just sets the table
and waits.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “barley harvest” (Ruth 1:22), what one honest sentence would you pray beside the table set before you after reading, “it just sets the table and waits”?
paintings.zh_poem:
她说她空手而归。
但看看谁走在她身边。

看看田野——
第一大麦弯曲黄金
他们到达的那个季节。

这个故事并没有与她的悲伤争论。
它只是摆设桌子
并等待。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼在“大麦收割”（路得记 1:22）时停下来时，读完“它只是摆好桌子并等待”之后，你会在摆在你面前的桌子旁祈祷哪一句诚实的句子？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们来到伯利恒时正是大麦收割的初期。”

paintings.title: as it happened
paintings.epigraph: “she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz”
paintings.poem:
she happened to come
to the field of Boaz.

the storyteller almost smiles.
happened.

as if a Moabite widow
wandering among strangers' fields
just chanced on the one man in Bethlehem
who was family.

call it luck
if you want.
the book has another name for it
and waits for you to notice.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“she happened to come to the field of Boaz”) and the closing thought (“the book has another name for it and waits for you to notice”), what is Ruth 2:3 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
她碰巧来了
到波阿斯的田地。

讲故事的人几乎笑了。
发生了。

就像摩押寡妇一样
徘徊在陌生的田野间
刚刚在伯利恒偶然遇见了一个人
谁是家人。

称之为运气
如果你愿意的话。
这本书还有另一个名字
并等待您的注意。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“她碰巧来到波阿斯的田地”）和结束语（“这本书有另一个名字，等待你去注意”）之间，路得记 2:3 在你那个时代温柔地重构了什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “她碰巧来到了波阿斯的田地”

paintings.title: the edges
paintings.epigraph: “let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves”
paintings.poem:
the law left the edges of the field
for the poor and the foreigner.

she was both.

so she bent where others had already been,
morning into afternoon,
picking up what fell.

not ashamed
to begin with leftovers.
so much grace
starts at the edges.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of Where You Go, “the edges” (Ruth 2:2–7) slows us down at the quiet centerpiece of “the edges” to remind us: “so much grace starts at the edges.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
法律离开了领域的边缘
对于穷人和外国人。

她两者都是。

所以她在其他人已经弯过的地方弯下腰，
从早上到下午，
捡起掉落的东西。

不感到羞耻
从剩菜开始。
如此多的恩典
从边缘开始。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 沿着《你去往何处》的道路，“边缘”（得2:2-7）让我们在“边缘”安静的中心放慢脚步，提醒我们：“如此多的恩典是从边缘开始的。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “让我在禾捆里追随收割者拾取麦穗”

paintings.title: the water jars
paintings.epigraph: “When you are thirsty, go to the vessels, and drink from that which the young men have drawn.”
paintings.poem:
he told the young men
to leave her alone.

he told her
the water was hers too.

it isn't the grand gesture
that changes a life.
it is someone with power
saying: you are safe here,
and there is enough to drink.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “the water jars” (Ruth 2:8–9), what would you talk about after reading, “it is someone with power saying: you are safe here, and there is enough to drink”?
paintings.zh_poem:
他告诉年轻人
让她独自一人。

他告诉她
水也是她的。

这不是一个伟大的举动
改变生活。
这是有权力的人
说：你在这里很安全，
而且有足够的喝的。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，并在“水缸”前停下来（路得记2:8-9），当你读到“有权力的人说：你在这里很安全，有足够的水喝”之后，你会谈论什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你们渴了，就到器皿那里去，喝年轻人打来的水。”

paintings.title: under his wings
paintings.epigraph: “under whose wings you have come to take refuge”
paintings.poem:
Boaz blessed her
with a picture:

a young bird
that has flown a long way
from the land of its birth,
tucked now
under the wings of the God of Israel.

he doesn't know yet
that he will be
the answer
to his own prayer.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the quiet centerpiece of “under his wings”: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “under his wings”—“he doesn't know yet that he will be the answer to his own prayer”?
paintings.zh_poem:
波阿斯祝福她
有图片：

一只幼鸟
已经飞了很远的路
来自它诞生的土地，
现在藏起来
在以色列神的翅膀之下。

他还不知道
他将成为
答案
为了他自己的祈祷。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“在他的翅膀下”的安静中心部分前停顿一下：今天，当你坐在“在他的翅膀下”的结束语——“他还不知道他会成为他自己祈祷的答案”时，你的姿势有什么变化？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你来到谁的庇护之下”

paintings.title: carry some home
paintings.epigraph: “She ate, was satisfied, and left some of it.”
paintings.poem:
at mealtime he called her over.
bread. a bowl to dip it in.
a handful of roasted grain
passed hand to hand.

she ate until she was full,
maybe for the first time in a long time,
and saved what was left
for Naomi.

that is how the hungry love:
eat,
then carry some home.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the daily loaf broken in the hand in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “that is how the hungry love: eat, then carry some home” (Ruth 2:14–18)?
paintings.zh_poem:
吃饭的时候他叫她过来。
面包。一个碗来蘸它。
一把烤谷物
手把手地传递。

她一直吃到吃饱为止
也许是很长一段时间以来的第一次，
并保存了剩下的东西
为了娜奥米.

这就是饥饿者的爱：
吃，
然后带一些回家。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画作中每天手中掰开的面包的宁静：当你思考“饥饿的人就是这样：吃，然后带一些回家”（得2:14-18）时，你能放下什么努力呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “她吃了，很满意，还留下了一些。”

paintings.title: one of ours
paintings.epigraph: “The man is a close relative to us, one of our near kinsmen.”
paintings.poem:
she came home at dusk
with an ephah of barley
and a name.

Boaz? Naomi said,
and something in her
that had lain still for years
sat up.

he's one of ours.
a kinsman.
one who can redeem.

the first hope in the book
arrives in a sack of grain
at the end of a long day.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Ruth 2:19–20, the story turns on the barley harvest—and ends with, “the first hope in the book arrives in a sack of grain at the end of a long day.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
她黄昏时回家
配一伊法大麦
和一个名字。

波阿斯？内奥米说，
和她身上的某些东西
已经静止多年
坐起来。

他是我们的一员。
一个亲戚。
一个可以救赎的人。

书中的第一个希望
装着一袋谷物到达
在漫长的一天结束时。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在路得记 2 章 19-20 节中，故事以大麦收割为话题，并以“书中第一个希望在漫长的一天结束时在一袋谷物中到来”作为结尾。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “这个人是我们的近亲，是我们的近亲之一。”

paintings.title: all that you say
paintings.epigraph: “All that you say, I will do.”
paintings.poem:
wash. anoint yourself.
put on your cloak.
go down to the floor.

it was a strange, brave plan,
older than we understand,
and Ruth trusted the woman
who had once said
call me bitter.

all that you say, I will do—

she said it the way
she had once said
your God, my God:
with her whole life.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The world measures life by speed and noise, yet Ruth 3:1–6 points us to the warm cloak and whispers, “all that you say, I will do— she said it the way she had once said your God, my God: with her whole life.” How can you practice that unhurried wisdom today?
paintings.zh_poem:
洗。膏抹自己。
穿上你的斗篷。
下到地板上。

这是一个奇怪而勇敢的计划，
比我们理解的更古老，
露丝信任这个女人
谁曾经说过
请叫我苦涩。

你所说的，我都会做——

她是这么说的
她曾经说过
你的上帝，我的上帝：
与她的一生。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 世界用速度和噪音来衡量生命，然而路得记 3:1-6 却向我们指出了温暖的斗篷，并低语道：“凡你所说的，我必遵行——她说这话的方式，就是她曾经用一生对你的神、我的神说的话。”今天你如何能修习这种从容的智慧呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你说什么，我就做什么。”

paintings.title: the heap of grain
paintings.epigraph: “he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain”
paintings.poem:
the harvest was in.
the work was done.
the heap of grain lay pale under the stars.

and a woman came softly
in the dark
to ask a question
without words.

the story tells it quietly.
so will we.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: The poem closes with a quiet turn: “the story tells it quietly. so will we.” Where in your life right now does that line hit closest to home?
paintings.zh_poem:
收获已经到来。
工作已经完成了。
星星下的谷物堆显得苍白。

一个女人轻轻走过来
在黑暗中
问一个问题
无言。

故事静静地讲述着。
我们也会。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 这首诗以安静的转折结束：“故事静静地讲述。我们也会。”现在，这条线在你生活中的哪个地方最贴近你的家？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他躺在粮堆的尽头”

paintings.title: the corner of the cloak
paintings.epigraph: “spread the corner of your garment over your servant; for you are a near kinsman.”
paintings.poem:
spread your wing over me,
she said—
the same word
he had used for God.

you prayed that I would find shelter
under his wings.
be the answer, Boaz.
be the corner of the cloak.

sometimes God's wings
look like a person
willing to be
the answer.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Sometimes a single sentence opens a window in a closed room: how does “sometimes God's wings look like a person willing to be the answer” (Ruth 3:9) speak to a question you have been carrying lately?
paintings.zh_poem:
张开你的翅膀覆盖我，
她说——
同一个词
他曾为上帝所用。

你祈祷我能找到庇护所
在他的羽翼之下。
波阿斯，就是答案。
成为斗篷的一角。

有时上帝的翅膀
看起来像一个人
愿意成为
答案。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 有时候，一句话就能在封闭的房间里打开一扇窗：“有时神的翅膀就像一个愿意解答问题的人”（路得记 3:9），这如何解答你最近一直在思考的一个问题？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “把衣角披在仆人身上，因为你们是至亲。”

paintings.title: a worthy woman
paintings.epigraph: “all the city of my people knows that you are a worthy woman.”
paintings.poem:
don't be afraid, he said.
everyone knows who you are.

not the Moabite.
not the widow.
not the foreigner at the edge of the field.

a worthy woman.

the town had been watching all along—
every sunrise in the barley,
every handful carried home—
and had quietly
changed her name.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Hold your hands open for a moment before “a worthy woman” (Ruth 3:10–11): what are you gripping tightly that loosens when you hear, “the town had been watching all along— every sunrise in the barley, every handful carried home— and had quietly changed her name”?
paintings.zh_poem:
别害怕，他说。
每个人都知道你是谁。

不是摩押人。
不是寡妇。
不是场边的外国人。

一个有价值的女人。

整个镇子一直在注视着——
大麦地里的每一个日出，
每一把都带回家——
并悄悄地
改变了她的名字。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“一位配得的妇人”面前张开你的双手（路得记3:10-11）：当你听到“全城一直在注视着大麦的每一次日出，每一捧都被带回家——并且悄悄地改变了她的名字”时，你紧握的是什么松开了？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “全城人民都知道你是一个值得尊敬的女人。”

paintings.title: not empty
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t go empty to your mother-in-law.”
paintings.poem:
he filled her mantle with barley
before the sun came up.

don't go back empty, he said—
not knowing
he was answering
the bitterest thing Naomi ever said.

empty is not
the last word.
it never was.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Scripture remembers this moment in Ruth 3:15–17 not to impress us, but to steady us: when have you seen the truth that “empty is not the last word. it never was” in your own story?
paintings.zh_poem:
他用大麦填满了她的斗篷
在太阳升起之前。

别空手而归，他说——
不知道
他正在回答
内奥米说过的最痛苦的话。

空不是
最后一句话。
从来没有。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 圣经在路得记 3 章 15-17 节中记住这一刻，不是为了给我们留下深刻印象，而是为了让我们坚定：你什么时候在你自己的故事中看到过“空虚不是最终的结论。它从来都不是”这个真理？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “别空去找你婆婆。”

paintings.title: wait
paintings.epigraph: “Wait, my daughter, until you know what will happen”
paintings.poem:
wait, my daughter.

the hardest part of hope
is the afternoon
after you have done everything you can.

the grain is measured.
the question is asked.
somewhere a man is walking to the gate.

sit down.
he will not rest
until it's settled.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: As your pilgrim lantern pauses at “wait” (Ruth 3:18), what one honest sentence would you pray beside the city gate after reading, “he will not rest until it's settled”?
paintings.zh_poem:
等等，我的女儿。

希望中最困难的部分
是下午
当你做了你能做的一切之后。

测量谷物。
问题被提出。
某处有一个人正走向大门。

坐下。
他不会休息
直到事情解决为止。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 当你的朝圣灯笼停在“等候”（路得记3:18）时，当你读到“事情不解决，他必不安息”之后，你会在城门旁祈祷哪一句诚实的句子呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “等等，我的女儿，直到你知道会发生什么”

paintings.title: at the gate
paintings.epigraph: “Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there.”
paintings.poem:
no swords, no speeches.
just a man at the gate
in the morning,
calling another man to sit,
gathering ten elders
as witnesses.

this is how redemption looks
in a small town:
a bargain spoken aloud,
patience,
and someone who shows up early.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Between the opening line (“no swords, no speeches”) and the closing thought (“this is how redemption looks in a small town: a bargain spoken aloud, patience, and someone who shows up early”), what is Ruth 4:1–2 gently reframing in your own day?
paintings.zh_poem:
没有剑，没有言语。
只是门口的一个人
早上，
叫另一个人坐下，
聚集十位长老
作为证人。

这就是救赎的样子
在一个小镇：
大声说出的讨价还价，
耐心，
和一个很早出现的人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在开场白（“没有刀剑，没有演讲”）和结束语（“这就是小镇里的救赎：大声讲出的交易、耐心和早到的人”）之间，路得记 4:1-2 在你那个时代温柔地重构了什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “波阿斯上到城门，就坐在那里。”

paintings.title: the sandal
paintings.epigraph: “a man took off his sandal, and gave it to his neighbor”
paintings.poem:
the nearer kinsman
wanted the field
but not the widow.

so he untied his sandal
and handed it over—
the old way of saying
this is yours now.

one man kept his inheritance safe.
the other gave himself away,
and his is the name
we still say.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Along the road of Where You Go, “the sandal” (Ruth 4:6–8) slows us down at the dust on your sandals to remind us: “the other gave himself away, and his is the name we still say.” Where are you being invited to trade control for trust today?
paintings.zh_poem:
近亲
想要这个领域
但寡妇却不然。

于是他解开了凉鞋
并把它交给了——
旧的说法
现在这是你的了。

一个人保护了他的遗产的安全。
另一个则暴露了自己，
这是他的名字
我们仍然说。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在《你去往何处》的路上，“凉鞋”（路得记 4：6-8）让我们因凉鞋上的灰尘而放慢脚步，提醒我们：“另一个人暴露了自己，而我们仍然说他的名字。”今天你被邀请在哪里用控制权换取信任？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “一个人脱下凉鞋，把它给了他的邻居”

paintings.title: we are witnesses
paintings.epigraph: “We are witnesses.”
paintings.poem:
we are witnesses,
said the whole gate.

they blessed a foreign woman
with the names of Rachel and Leah,
the mothers who built the house of Israel.

a Moabite
written into the family prayer.

that is the kind of house
God builds:
the door stays open
long after
you'd think it would close.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: If you were walking this road with a close friend and stopped at “we are witnesses” (Ruth 4:9–12), what would you talk about after reading, “that is the kind of house God builds: the door stays open long after you'd think it would close”?
paintings.zh_poem:
我们是见证人，
整个城门都说道。

他们祝福一位外国妇女
以雷切尔和利亚的名字命名，
建造以色列家的母亲们。

摩押人
写进家庭祈祷文。

这就是那种房子
神建造：
门一直开着
很久之后
你会认为它会关闭。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 如果你和一位亲密的朋友一起走在这条路上，并在“我们是见证人”（路得记 4：9-12）处停了下来，那么在读到“这就是上帝建造的房子：门在你以为它会关上很久之后，门却一直开着”之后，你会谈论什么？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “我们是见证人。”

paintings.title: a son
paintings.epigraph: “Yahweh enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.”
paintings.poem:
after ten empty years in Moab,
a son.

the book is careful
to say who gave him:
the Lord.

every birth is a gift.
this one
was also an answer.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Pause before the quiet centerpiece of “a son”: what changes in your posture today when you sit with the closing words of “a son”—“this one was also an answer”?
paintings.zh_poem:
在摩押度过了空虚的十年之后，
一个儿子。

书很仔细
说谁给了他：
主啊。

每一次出生都是一份礼物。
这个
也是一个答案。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在“一个儿子”这个安静的中心人物前停下来：今天，当你坐在“一个儿子”的结束语——“这也是一个答案”时，你的姿势有什么变化？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “耶和华使她怀孕，生了一个儿子。”

paintings.title: full
paintings.epigraph: “your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons”
paintings.poem:
the women gathered around Naomi
and counted it out like a blessing:

a restorer of life.
a nurse for your old age.
a daughter-in-law who loves you,
better than seven sons.

she laid the child in her lap,
the woman who had come home empty,

and her arms
were full.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: Look at the stillness of the quiet centerpiece of “full” in Timothy’s painting: what striving can you lay down as you ponder, “she laid the child in her lap, the woman who had come home empty, and her arms were full” (Ruth 4:14–16)?
paintings.zh_poem:
妇女们聚集在拿俄米周围
并将其视为祝福：

生命的恢复者。
为你的晚年做一名护士。
一个爱你的儿媳妇，
胜过七个儿子。

她把孩子放在腿上，
空手而归的女人，

和她的手臂
已经满了。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 看看提摩太画作中安静的中心“满”的宁静：当你沉思“她把孩子放在膝上，这个空着回家的女人，她的怀里满了”（路得记4：14-16）时，你能放下什么努力？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “你的儿媳妇，她爱你，对你比七个儿子更好”

paintings.title: the family line
paintings.epigraph: “They named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.”
paintings.poem:
the neighbors named him.
a son is born to Naomi, they said.

Obed.
father of Jesse.
grandfather of a shepherd boy
who would be king.

and from there the line runs on,
generation after generation,
to another child
in the House of Bread.

a famine, a funeral, a foreigner, a field—
and out of it,
the family of the Messiah.
paintings.reflectionPrompt: In Ruth 4:17, the story turns on the daily loaf broken in the hand—and ends with, “a famine, a funeral, a foreigner, a field— and out of it, the family of the Messiah.” What small, unhurried faithfulness is God inviting you into today?
paintings.zh_poem:
邻居给他起了名字。
他们说，内奥米生了一个儿子。

奥贝德。
杰西的父亲。
牧童的祖父
谁会成为国王。

线路从那里继续延伸，
一代又一代，
给另一个孩子
在面包之家。

饥荒、葬礼、外国人、田野——
从中，
弥赛亚的家人。
paintings.zh_reflectionPrompt: 在路得记 4 章 17 节中，故事以每日用手擘开的面包展开，并以“饥荒、葬礼、外邦人、田地——从中诞生了弥赛亚的家人”结束。神今天邀请你进入什么样的小而从容的信实呢？
paintings.zh_epigraph: “他们给他起名叫俄备得。他是耶西的父亲，大卫的父亲。”

zh_beforeYouBegin: 路得是一个关于饥荒、三场葬礼、一个外国寡妇和一片大麦地的短篇故事。到了最后一页，一座空荡荡的房子已经住满了，一条家族血脉向大卫延伸。本书共分为四章，二十四首短诗。每首诗都位于一幅画旁边和一行经文之下。
